verdict.rationale: Vapi documents an official CLI and an official MCP server, both stated to manage assistants, phone numbers, and calls, so a coding agent can work with all three objects without the dashboard; the server SDK also creates assistants in code. However, the docs only say these surfaces 'manage' these objects, so the specific steps of attaching a number to an assistant and placing an outbound call are implied rather than shown, and the quickstarts are dashboard-driven. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of programmatic number provisioning/attachment and outbound call placement via CLI/MCP, an end-to-end headless walkthrough, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my coding agent can provision a complete voice agent end to end — create the agent, attach a number, and place a call — through the API, CLI, or MCP without touching the dashboard

citations.quote: Manage assistants, phone numbers, and calls from your terminal
The Vapi MCP Server exposes Vapi APIs as tools via the Model Context Protocol (MCP), so you can manage assistants, phone numbers, and calls from any MCP-compatible AI assistant
